title: HA scan: single-instance operator database and unspread replicas
description: Asked whether databases are highly available. ledger-db is a single-instance operator cluster, redis is one replica, api has 3 replicas with no spread. Everything is Running, which is the trap: running is not highly available.
prompt: Are my databases highly available? What would break if a node died?

live.availability:
VERDICT WITHIN READABLE RESOURCES: 2 workloads are single points of failure (single replica/instance); 1 multi-replica workloads lack anti-affinity/topology-spread (replicas can co-locate). Healthy is not the same as highly available.

Availability / single-point-of-failure scan (redundancy, not just health):

SINGLE POINTS OF FAILURE (2), one replica/instance, so a pod or node loss takes them down:
  - Cluster data/ledger-db (postgresql.cnpg.io): instances=1, single instance, no redundancy
  - Deployment cache/redis: 1 replica, no redundancy

NOT TRULY HIGHLY AVAILABLE (1), multiple replicas but nothing forces them onto different nodes/zones:
  - Deployment shop/api: 3 replicas but no pod anti-affinity or topology-spread, all replicas can land on one node/zone

Redundant workloads (>1 replica): 1
PodDisruptionBudgets in cluster: 2 (a PDB can't protect a single-replica workload, evicting its one pod always violates availability).
Notes: DaemonSets are per-node by design and excluded. Operator custom resources are matched generically by a replica/instance field, so an operator using an unusual field name may be missed, use list_resources/get_resource to confirm. True HA also needs replicas actually spread across nodes/zones and, for stateful data, automated failover.

mustMatch.desc: says ledger-db is a single instance / single point of failure
states the databases are NOT highly available
flags that api has replicas but no anti-affinity or topology spread

mustNotMatch.desc: does not claim the databases are highly available
